record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does the undirected s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to deterministic logspace L, preferably avoiding the heavier machinery used in existing proofs?

evidence.quote: Can reusing space be used to give a simpler, more efficient deterministic algorithm for uSTConn? ... Problem 1. Give a simple, direct proof of uSTConn ∈ L.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let uSTConn denote the following decision problem: given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ and two vertices $s,t\in V$, decide whether there exists a path in $G$ from $s$ to $t$. Let $\mathsf{L}$ denote the class of decision problems solvable by a deterministic Turing machine using $O(\log n)$ space on inputs of length $n$.

It is known that $\text{uSTConn}\in\mathsf{L}$; the existing proofs proceed via constructions of expander graphs (e.g., the zig-zag product) and amplify spectral expansion through a logarithmic number of phases, which is technically heavy.

Problem: Provide a simple, direct proof that $\text{uSTConn}\in\mathsf{L}$, i.e., exhibit a deterministic logspace algorithm for undirected $s$-$t$ connectivity together with a correctness and space-complexity analysis that avoids the heavy machinery of expander constructions and the zig-zag (or related) product.
artifact.status_search_result: The only known proofs that undirected s-t connectivity lies in deterministic logspace (Reingold 2005/2008, and subsequent variants by Rozenman–Vadhan via derandomized squaring) all rely on expander-graph machinery such as the zig-zag product or derandomized squaring. No qualitatively simpler, direct logspace algorithm for uSTConn appears to be known in the literature, so the question of finding such a proof remains open.

status_evidence.title: Undirected Connectivity in Log-Space (Reingold)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm uses zig-zag product to transform graph into expanders in logarithmically many phases.
status_evidence.claim: The standard proof of uSTConn in L relies on expander constructions and the zig-zag product.

status_evidence.title: SL (complexity) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Reingold's 2005 proof that SL=L uses the zig-zag graph product; no simpler direct proof has superseded it.
status_evidence.claim: The known proofs of uSTConn ∈ L use heavy expander/zig-zag machinery.
